::: {.why}
It is the statistic clients ask for and the one with the worst sampling properties in common use, and treating it as a parameter rather than as a realisation is the mistake that produces confident nonsense.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Given a Sharpe ratio and a horizon, simulate the distribution of maximum drawdown and report its interquartile range.
- Say why maximum drawdown grows with sample length even for a strategy whose properties have not changed.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Simulate the distribution: 10,000 paths at a true Sharpe of 1 over three years of daily returns, and plot the histogram of maximum drawdown. Report the median and the 5th and 95th percentiles. The width of that interval is the answer to almost every question anyone asks about a drawdown.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Show the length dependence: repeat at one, three, five and ten years and plot median maximum drawdown against horizon. Then reconcile your five SPY numbers from last night with the pattern.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add `max_drawdown()` and `drawdown_series()` to qlib/stats.py, with a test on a hand-constructed path whose answer you can verify by eye.
:::
:::
